CT-xCOV adopts an end-to-end approach from lung segmentation to COVID-19 detection and explanations of the detection model’s prediction. For lung segmentation, we used the well-known U-Net model. For COVID-19 detection, we compared three different CNN architectures: a standard CNN, ResNet50, and DenseNet121. After the detection, visual and textual explanations are provided. For visual explanations, we applied three different XAI techniques, namely, Grad-Cam, Integrated Gradient (IG), and LIME. Textual explanations are added by computing the percentage of infection by lungs. To assess the performance of the used XAI techniques, we propose a ground-truth-based evaluation method, measuring the similarity between the visualization outputs and the ground-truth infections. The performed experiments show that the applied DL models achieved good results. The U-Net segmentation model achieved a high Dice coefficient (98%). The performance of our proposed classification model (standard CNN) was validated using 5-fold cross-validation (acc of 98.40% and f1-score 98.23%). Lastly, the results of the comparison of XAI techniques show that Grad-Cam gives the best explanations compared to LIME and IG, by achieving a Dice coefficient of 55%, on COVID-19 positive scans, compared to 29% and 24% obtained by IG and LIME respectively. The code and the dataset used in this paper are available in the GitHub repository [1].

articleTitle: NF-NIDS: Normalizing Flows for Network Intrusion Detection Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: The rising frequency and complexity of cyber threats have necessitated the development of effective Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS). Anomaly-based detection approaches have gained prominence for their ability to detect unknown and sophisticated attacks. In this paper, we introduce NF-NIDS, a novel approach for anomaly-based network intrusion detection using Normalizing Flows (NFs) to accurately classify network traffic into normal or malicious categories given the assumption of the availability of scarce attack samples. To address the challenge of limited attack samples, we employ two flow-based models, namely Inverse Autoregressive Flow (IAF) and Neural Spline Flows (NSF). These models are used to learn the underlying distribution of normal traffic and generate pseudo-attacks from the tails of the distribution. To evaluate the effectiveness of NF-NIDS, we conducted experiments on three well-known network datasets. The results demonstrate that our approach achieves high performance levels while incurring low to negligible false discovery rates. Specifically, NF-NIDS yields impressive results, with an accuracy of 98.71% for USTC-TFC2016, 94.86% for CIC-IDS2017, and 98.20% for CIC-IDS2018. In terms of the F1-score, NF-NIDS scores 98.72% for USTC-TFC2016, 97.05% for CIC-IDS2017, and 99.51% for CIC-IDS2018.

articleTitle: Attack and anomaly detection in IoT Networks using machine learning approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: The rapid expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) gives Intruders a wide attack surface from which they can conduct more damaging cyber-attacks. Scan, Spying, Denial of Service, Data Type Probing, Malicious Control, and Malicious Operation are such attacks and anomalies that can bring down an IoT system, which makes Attack and anomaly detection in IoT a rising concern and creating a powerful Intrusion Detection System (IDS) a primary need. The main goal of an intrusion detection system (IDS) is detecting attacks and any attempt to break down networks. Machine learning techniques have recently been used in intrusion detection systems since they have shown the ability to learn and adapt, besides providing a quick response. This work proposes an intrusion detection framework that can classify network activities as “Normal” or “Attack” using various machine learning methods. A common dataset called BoT-IoT evaluated the suggested model using KNIME analytics Platform.

articleTitle: Augmented Reality with Mobility Awareness in Mobile Edge Computing over 6G Network: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Augmented reality (AR) technology is an advancement that allows users to see the real world through the use of a virtual device. The explosive manufacturing of mobile devices follows a rise in the popularity of mobile phones and allows the user to run AR applications based on the mobile with substantial mobility awareness. The new generation networking technology (e.g., 6G) serves as a challenge for upcoming AR applications to attain low latency and computationally enhanced during the time that mobile edge computing (MEC) allows the user to communicate easily with AR applications. However, previous work on mobile edge computing support AR may not perform as expected in many practical cases, such as irreparable network interruptions due to wireless connectivity instability and user mobility, which is defining feature of popular AR applications. To attain low latency, deploying computational and mobility, the MEC will perform a major role in either fifth generation (5G) or six-generation (6G) networking. This paper studies in general the AR concept and the utility of mobility management in MEC applications that can be implemented in the next generation of mobile by reviewing the user to connect their interface. This paper discusses augmented reality and mobility challenges. The future direction and solution for the implementation of AR based mobility aware and MEC are also analyzed. This survey will contribute a comprehensive of the issues associated with mobility management, specifically concerning augmented reality with mobility awareness in future.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Survey On Efficient Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: In recent years, there has been substantial attention directed towards the development of proficient Transformers, which display considerable potential in effectively managing extensive sequences in various fields, including but not limited to natural language processing and computer vision. While researchers have conducted survey papers on this field, there remains a notable gap in papers that specifically present and discuss benchmark datasets tailored to evaluate the efficiency and performance of efficient transformers in specific challenges, notably hierarchical reasoning on long-range sequences, question answering on large documents, and key phrase extraction. Moreover, our paper aims to fill this void by offering a clear and comprehensive survey of efficient Transformers. We focus on three main approaches: sparse attention, linearized attention, and low rank attention, all geared towards mitigating the computational and memory challenges associated with traditional Transformers while ensuring consistently high-performance levels. By presenting and analyzing these critical aspects, our paper endeavors to contribute to the broader understanding and advancements in efficient Transformers, paving the way for further research and innovation in this dynamic field.

articleTitle: Traffic Monitoring Using IoT And Lambda Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to conduct a study on traffic congestion and road activity monitoring, as one solution among others in the field of Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS). It presents the idea of the system as a prototype using Java simulation programs and simple IoT sensors, leading to a complete national safety system using high-tech physical devices, sensors placed at the roadside, traffic lights as well as on compatible vehicles. In addition, Big Data technologies play a major role in the system, through the use of RabbitMQ, Spark and MongoDB. The approach highlights the real-time processing aspect with the aim of having user-friendly processing given that transport is a major problem in everyday life that requires on-the-fly processing, hence the use of Spark live streaming rather than batch processing. Data integrity and availability are emphasized, as is the use of machine learning for knowledge extraction. All these factors were taken into account in the processing and storage sections. The results obtained show that the choices made are largely judicious and have achieved acceptable accuracy in terms of data volume, variety and speed.

articleTitle: Seizure Detection using Machine Learning and Monitoring through IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Rapid and erratic electrical firing in the brain is what causes seizures. This may result in momentary anomalous behaviors, movements (such as jerky, alternately stiffened arms and legs), sensations, or unconsciousness or an altered degree of consciousness. According to a survey, approximately 50 million people around the world suffer from epilepsy, making it one of the most common neurological diseases on a global scale. Despite modern pharmacological and surgical treatment options, more than a quarter of epilepsy patients experience uncontrollable seizures. Early detection of seizures aids in the prevention of SUDEP (Sudden Unexpected Death in Epilepsy) This model proposed a machine learning approach to detect the seizure. The Random Forest Classifier algorithm was used to diagnose the seizure that was brought to our attention. A pretrained model with a machine learning and supervised classification approach is built with the datasets received from the EEG (electroencephalogram) and ECG (electrocardiogram) to detect seizures in the pre-ictal stage. The model has been trained with existing datasets, and the research shows that there are several causes of epilepsy. Even if the causes differ, the solution is the same. In this case, the model predicts the seizure and alerts the hospital management, nurses, and carers before it occurs. Which would be extremely beneficial to doctors in treating it.

articleTitle: Literature Review of Handover Decision Algorithms in 5G Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: As data traffic and mobile device usage continue to surge, ensuring the provision of reliable and stable services becomes paramount. While 5G networks hold the promise of addressing capacity limitations, they also present challenges in optimizing handover processes. This paper undertakes a review of contemporary handover decision algorithms within the 5G context, categorizing them based on their decision-making procedures, streamlining input parameters, evaluating performance, and elucidating employed strategies. This study provides a generalized depiction of the handover decision mechanism within 5G networks, thereby supporting the evolution of advanced handover optimization methods.

articleTitle: AI-Enabled Routing in Next-Gen Networks: A Brief Overview
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: The ever-increasing adoption of intelligent devices and diverse network technologies has led to a tremendous surge in data traffic, necessitating enhanced network performance in terms of coverage, capacity, latency, and reliability for large-scale applications. However, traditional routing protocols struggle to cope with the complexities of next-gen networks like 6G and satellite networks. To address these challenges, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine-learning (ML) techniques have emerged as promising solutions. This paper focuses exclusively on AI techniques applied to routing in next-gen networks, exploring the reasons behind AI’s significance in network optimization. The study delves into cognitive intelligence, knowledge planes, and the role of Software-Defined Networking (SDN). Challenges and potential solutions are discussed, highlighting the use of AI to optimize network performance and adaptability. The paper also presents an overview of AI methods and studies on AI-based routing solutions. Future research directions are suggested to pave the way for more efficient and reliable network infrastructures.

articleTitle: Combining Deep CNNs and Superpixels for Polyp Segmentation in Colonoscopy Images
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Polyps can be missed as a result of fatigue or inattention during prolonged or consecutive colonoscopies, with an estimated average rate of 16.8-28%. Consequently, patients with undetected polyps are less likely to survive late-stage colorectal cancer than those without polyps. The detection of polyps in colonoscopy images has been automated using a variety of approaches in order to address this issue. As a result, polyps will be prevented from being overlooked by humans, and the time and expense associated with screening numerous colonoscopies or wireless capsule endoscopies will be reduced. Our primary goal is to develop a system that precisely defines the location of polyps on an image, therefore increasing overall detection accuracy and enabling timely identification of colorectal cancer. In this work, we aim to combine UNet architecture with the pretrained model Inception-Resnet-V2 in the Encoder, and then a phase of segmentation Refinement based superpixels with Simple Linear Iterative Clustering (SLIC) for superpixels generation. The proposed methods’ average Dice on CVC-Clinic612 dataset is 0.8903, with MIoU and MPA of 0.8085 and 0.9796 respectively, and the average Dice on Kvasir-SEG dataset is 0.8758 with MIoU and MPA of 0.7936 and 0.9567 respectively. Comparing the results to state-of-the-art methods, the results show high performance.

articleTitle: Evaluation of User Allocation Techniques in Massive MIMO 5G Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Massive MIMO (Multiple Input Multiple Output) is a fundamental technique for improving the efficiency of 5G wireless networks. At the base station, it calls for the use of numerous antennas—usually in the dozens or even hundreds. In addition to better coverage and less interference, this enables a large increase in the amount of data that can be delivered and received simultaneously. By enabling more precise signal transmission and reception, Massive MIMO can also result in significant energy savings. The use of optimization techniques can further improve the performance of 5G networks. The aim of this paper is to investigate a signal quality optimization technique for MIMO in which users are allocated to antennas according to different algorithms. For our research, the DeepMIMO simulator produced a dataset that sets up all necessary parameters. In our study, we examine different techniques for user allocation in 5G MIMO Networks. We conclude that transforming the problem of user allocation to a linear assignment problem in order to find the most efficient connection between the users and the base stations is one of the best ways to optimize user allocation.

articleTitle: Review of Free Space Optical Communication: Advantages and Disadvantages
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Free-space optical communication (FSO) is a revolutionary technology that utilizes optical signals to transmit data wirelessly, providing a viable alternative to conventional wired systems. This paper aims to explore the FSO system, analyze previous research, and discuss the challenges associated with information transmission in FSO networks, particularly under adverse weather conditions that can lead to weakened signals. FSO technology has garnered significant attention due to its numerous advantages, such as high data rates, quick installation, cost-effectiveness, and enhanced security. Many researchers have delved into this field, contributing valuable insights and advancements in the FSO domain. However, one of the major challenges faced by FSO systems is their sensitivity to weather conditions in the vicinity of the transmitter site. Adverse weather factors, such as rain, fog, snow, and dust, can attenuate the optical signals, leading to a reduction in signal strength and potentially affecting data transmission reliability.

articleTitle: Access Control for Collaboration in Cloud Environment: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Collaborative systems enable users to collaborate on shared tasks using distributed platforms. In such collaborations, cloud-based solutions are commonly used to store data and capitalize on cloud computing advantages. However, participants may need access to resources controlled by other collaborators, including sensitive data. Ensuring access control for collaboration and cross-tenant access in multi-cloud environment is a crucial challenge to address. This paper provides an in-depth exploration of access control models in multi-tenant environments, specifically for collaboration scenarios involving tenants from the same or different clouds. Each model is comprehensively explained, emphasizing its advantages and limitations. Additionally, a comparative analysis of the discussed access control models is included. Based on this study, we propose guidelines for implementing effective access control, carefully considering the specific authorization requirements for cross-tenant access in a multi-cloud environment.

articleTitle: Neighborhood Feature Extraction and Haralick Attributes for Medical Image Analysis: Application to Breast Cancer Mammography Image
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: This paper describes a new preprocessing method using Markovian modification to distinguish preprocessed mammograms (healthy and pathological), and these techniques are very necessary to find the direction of mammograms so that we can eliminate noise, improve image quality and obtaining more appropriate images than the original images as well as the disappearance of misplaced discrete points. Markovian image segmentation was performed to extract the region of the blocks if the blocks ended up being divided into groups of pixels that are homogeneous with the image with respect to certain criteria, based on the neighborhood system, using a relaxation approach that It is maintained by iterative conditional patterns (ICM), relying on an energy function adapted to the irregular neighborhood models of the image, and with the energy criterion of the image groups, the neighborhood system, and some cluster groups. These preprocessed mammograms are analyzed using co-occurrence matrices from which Haralick traits are extracted. The peculiarity of this approach is that it selects features from among the most selective mammograms based on the type of contact chosen for preprocessing. The most discriminating features are selected according to a supervised scheme that makes it possible to represent mammograms in a relatively small space where they can be discriminated with high reliability. To test this method and verify its validity, we use mammograms of normal and sick cases from the Reference Center for Reproductive Health in Kenitra, Morocco (CRSRKM).

articleTitle: IA Applied to IIoT Intrusion Detection: An Overview
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Over years, the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has evolved rapidly, offering increased connectivity and benefits in terms of efficiency and productivity as well as significant business opportunities. It is used in various fields such as transportation, production, supply chain management, the oil and gas sector, mining and metallurgy, energy services, aviation, etc. However, this increased connectivity also exposes industrial systems to greater security risks, including intrusion attempts and cyberattacks. The multitude of sensors present in these networks generates a considerable amount of data, attracting the attention of cybercriminals worldwide. To protect Industrial Internet of Things networks, applications against these attacks and intrusion detection systems play a crucial role. However, they have limitations in terms of detection accuracy and false alert management. By using machine learning and deep learning techniques, it is possible to mitigate the multiple security threats and enhance the ability of intrusion detection systems to identify complex attacks patterns and to adapt configurations against new threats. Indeed, such artificial intelligence methods can analyze vast amounts of real-time data, detect anomalies, identify known attack signatures and even predict potential attacks. This article constitutes a bibliographical overview of artificial intelligence based intrusion detection approaches as well as the different datasets on which they have been tested. Additionally, it aims to identify current limitations and challenges in ongoing and existing researches and solutions, while providing some directions for further scientific works.

articleTitle: Proposed Sentiment Analysis of COVID-19 Tweets using Machine Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Social media coverage of COVID-19 has facilitated the analysis of pandemic sentiment through the application of various Machine Learning Algorithms. Twitter is a prominent a social media platform where individuals share tweets related to COVID-19, such as the count of positive cases or deaths, inducing a surge of apprehension and anxiety gripping individuals worldwide. This presents a chance for researchers and data analysts to acquire data intended for scholarly and research objectives. Primary objective of this study is to evaluate the accuracy of sentiment analysis of people’s perceptions regarding COVID-19 related news. We gathered Twitter data by focusing on hashtag keywords related to the coronavirus, COVID-19, new case, and deaths. The data was categorized into positive or negative categories utilized machine learning algorithms, including the multilayer perceptron, naive Bayes, random forest, and support vector machine, for the classification process. The algorithms were compared for accuracy using the datasets. All of the algorithms demonstrated a high degree of accuracy in their predictions, with the support vector machine algorithm achieving the highest classification accuracy of 99%. Consequently, the findings demonstrate that 70% of the sentiments exhibited positivity, while the remaining 30% conveyed negativity.

articleTitle: Smart Parking System Approaches and Positioning Technologies: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: In the realm of the smart city concept, every aspect of urban life is set to become intelligent, spanning across buildings, manufacturing, healthcare, agriculture, and transportation. A crucial component of the transportation system within the smart city framework is the implementation of smart parking systems. This particular aspect has garnered considerable attention from researchers,industries,and all stakeholders involved in shaping and developing the smart city vision. Currently, a diverse array of smart parking solutions is being introduced to the market by solution providers, employing various innovative approaches.Guidance is a key component in smart parking solution, we distinguish two guidance systems: External guidance and Internal guidance. External guidance help car drivers to reach a parking zone while Internal guidance gives instructions for drivers to find parking spot inside the parking space. The primary objective of this paper is to explore the smart parking domain from three distinct perspectives: i) an overview of the latest existing approaches to parking management, ii) external positioning and guidance methods for smart parking, and iii) an in-depth survey of the most widely utilized internal positioning technologies. The state of the art related to guidance in smart parking address internal and external guidance separately. we introduce in this paper the basics of our future work in which we will combine external and internal parking guidance to provide an end-to-end guidance service for smart parking users.

articleTitle: Blockchain-based spam detection approach
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Maintaining privacy is increasingly important for OSN (Online social network) users due to the massive quantity of sensitive shared data and the growing popularity of OSNs. Social media is now widely used and crucial for, networking, and communication. However, the widespread use of social media platforms has created numerous problems for modern society and industry. For instance, they disseminate spam data on social media because the network lacks the capability to do so. Social network platforms have revolutionized the way we communicate and interact with each other. However, the widespread use of social media has also led to an increase in spamming activities. Spamming refers to the distribution of unsolicited and irrelevant content that is intended to mislead or deceive users. In this article, we propose a blockchain-based approach for detecting spams in social media using bi-directional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) networks. We get a highly compelling and intriguing outcome with higher accuracy (97 percent) and lesser loss than typical learning algorithms

articleTitle: Internet of Things Systems Security Based on the Physical Objects: An overview
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: In the Internet of Things (IoT), physical objects are connected to the Internet and can collect, transmit, and receive data. Advances in microelectronics technology have led to smaller and more diverse IoT devices with increased capabilities. Cloud and edge technologies are also providing these devices with efficient computing, storage, and low-latency solutions. This has led to the widespread use of IoT in a variety of areas, but it also presents an increased risk of cyberattacks, data breaches, and unauthorized access to sensitive information. However, studies and analyses of physical object security and privacy in the IoT focus on identifying and mitigating these risks. This paper studied the challenges of IoT systems and different security requirements. On the other hand, the mapping of attack methods, architecture, and security measures of physical components in IoT systems Privacy, security, and architecture requirements will be associated with physical components based on their life cycles.

articleTitle: Tree-Driven Intelligent Security System for Intrusion Detection in IoT environment
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: With the rise of the Internet of Things (IoT), which envisions a connected network of intelligent devices communicating autonomously through the Internet, the need to deal with escalating threats and cyberattacks in these diverse environments becomes crucial. Detecting network intrusions that may indicate such attacks becomes imperative. However, machine learning (ML) techniques have proven their effectiveness in this regard by accurately detecting such anomalies. This paper presents a clever new intrusion detection system (IDS) designed to improve security in IoT networks, utilizing tree-structured ML models. Experimentation and evaluation of the IDS on well-established datasets demonstrates its capability to effectively detect and identify diverse cyberattacks with an increased detection rate and minimal computational costs.

articleTitle: The Influence of Spirituality Perspective on Internal Business Process in Private Universities
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: In organisational performance strategies, it has been established that Spirituality and religion workplace are emerging areas of research that are yet to be fully investigated. In addition, the influence of spirituality perspective on the general workforce seems not to be fully appreciated. Moreover, the Internal Business Perspective (IBP) also influences the successful implementation of organizational strategic goals, particularly with respect to its non-financial status. However, how workplace spirituality influences the IBP, and their incorporation are also part of the research trends that are yet to be thoroughly done, particularly concerning Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) and Private Universities (PUs). This study, therefore, examines the influence of spirituality on IBP in Yemen’s HEIs and PUs. To achieve this, an instrument based on Partial Least Square-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) was designed and administered to the PUs faculties in Yemen. The outcome of the analysis revealed showed that spirituality positively impacts IBP in Yemeni PUs. Therefore, this study would help in re-positioning the roles of spirituality in the general organizational performance, attaining the desired strategic success while having a fostered IBP capability for their workforce.

articleTitle: Indexation techniques in decision support systems: Study and Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: The query optimization process is the big challenge of most of decision support systems around the world, such systems based on data warehouse structure to store all data to be analyzed. Moreover, the volume and variety of data on the data warehouse are very important which involves more effort and investment to minimize the cost of refreshment and data update. Our aim in this paper is to describe the state of the art of research works dealing with the optimization approaches in big data environments especially, the techniques based on indexes selection problems. We will explain the principle of each technique and its particularities approved by our experimental data. In addition, we’ll conclude by the comparison of all these approaches developed in the literature.

articleTitle: Usage of Machine Learning in DDOS Attack Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: In this article, the best model for determining DDoS attacks using machine learning algorithms is proposed. During the research work, models were built using algorithms such as RFC (Random Forest Classifier), Logistic Regression, SVM (Support Vector Machine), KNN (k-Nearest Neighbor) and Decision Tree Classifier. A comparative analysis of each model was carried out with the reduction of their metrics, as a result of which the model with the best results was selected, showing the accuracy of the tests at 0.9995.

articleTitle: Evolution of Image Captioning Models: An Overview
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: This article presents a state-of-the-art review of image captioning methodologies developed in the past five years. Image captioning, which aims to generate text describing the visual content of an image, has gained increasing interest in the field of artificial intelligence. The article analyzes how image captioning methods have evolved, transitioning from traditional machine learning-based approaches to deep learning-based methods that have become dominant due to their effectiveness in efficiently extracting image features. The article also explores two main approaches to image captioning: dense (region-based) captioning and whole-scene captioning. It discusses approaches based on visual space and multimodal space for text generation. Furthermore, the article examines reinforcement learning methods, semantic enhancements, the use of self-attention transformer models, and pretrained models such as the Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT) that have improved the performance of image captioning. Finally, the article highlights various applications of this technique, including human-machine interaction, biomedicine, automatic medical prescription, children’s education, industrial quality control, traffic data analysis, and assistive technologies for visually impaired individuals.

articleTitle: Wireless Sensor Network for Water Salinization Monitoring in Irrigation of Vertical Farming
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: The importance of vertical farming is increasing day by day, given its numerous benefits including the possibility to cultivate a crop in the minimum available space. Similarly, the primary sector also needs technology incorporation to ensure sustainability. Therefore, this paper presents the design and deployment of a wireless sensor network (WSN) responsible for monitoring the quality of irrigation water in terms of salinization for vertical farming. The study presents 2 prototypes of salinity sensors, based on a single coil, which can determine the salt levels of the liquid in which they are introduced. Both prototypes are tested and compared with professional equipment, and then subjected to a validation process. Finally, the network traffic generated by such an installation for different numbers of nodes is analyzed, and the results show that the bandwidth consumed by a node like ESP32 is extremely low, with average bandwidth values of around 700 Bps.

articleTitle: IoT Integration in Agriculture: Advantages, Challenges, and Future Perspectives: Short survey
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: The era of the Internet of Things (IoT) has commenced, captivating us with the extensive application of futuristic technologies in the realm of smart farming. Various methods for enhancing agricultural tasks are actively under development to meet the burgeoning demand for food production. The maintenance and monitoring of farms have advanced significantly, the adoption of IoT-based alternatives to traditional human-driven tasks is rapidly getting more importance. Io T integrates a diverse range of technologies to elevate production and management within the agricultural sector. This survey delves into numerous advantages and challenges associated to integrating IoT technology in agricultural process. We present a collection of applications, an IoT architecture elucidating all its components, and a roster of protocols that enhance network performance. Furthermore, we discuss future prospective directions, placing emphasis on 5G, robotics, UAVs, and Big Data.

articleTitle: Real-time Tracking of Auditing Process Progress with a Customizable Application for Cybersecurity Standards Compliance: A Case Study on ISO 27001 and TISAX
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Certifications such as ISO 27001 and TISAX are crucial for organizations seeking to bolster cybersecurity and protect against evolving cyber threats. However, the process of obtaining these certifications involves navigating a rigorous auditing process fraught with challenges. This research paper addresses the difficulties faced by auditors in adapting to constant updates in regulatory requirements, relying on static tools during the gap analysis stage, and managing effective communication and collaboration with clients. Additionally, challenges in real-time tracking of client progress, document management, and generating on-demand reports further complicate the auditing process.To overcome these obstacles, this study introduces AUTOSYS as a proposed solution, detailing the technologies employed, the audit process, the web application architecture, and the implemented security measures. AUTOSYS is a highly customizable web application, for real-time audit monitoring. By leveraging real-time notifications and enabling continuous tracking of audited company activities, including tasks, incidents, and risks. The application incorporates a personalized checklist that adapts to norm requirement updates, thereby facilitating enhanced evaluation of norm compliance and maturity. Furthermore, the proposed solution streamlines audits by effectively managing shared checklists, ensuring efficient document management, and upholding privacy controls.

articleTitle: Improving Accuracy in Cloud Service Provider Ranking: Integrating TOPSIS with CAIQ-based QoS Assessment
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: The search for a reliable cloud service provider has become increasingly complex due to the increasing reliance on them. Researchers have developed a multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) method, including the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) for ranking. However, the selection process often relies on only a few aspects of service quality, known as Quality of Service (QoS) parameters. This research proposes a comprehensive methodology, using the Consensus Assessment Initiative Questionnaire (CAIQ) to select standardized QoS parameters and then applying the MCDM method, incorporating TOPSIS, to rank cloud service providers based on their performance. This approach aims to improve the accuracy and reliability of the selection process, enabling individuals and organizations to confidently identify and choose the most trustworthy cloud service providers for their specific needs.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of the performance of four learning models for predicting blood glucose levels in type 1 diabetic patients based on blood glucose measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Type 1 diabetes requires rigorous blood glucose management to prevent complications. Predicting future blood glucose levels is crucial. This study compares four learning models to forecast blood glucose levels based on current measurements. The literature review focuses on predicting blood glucose in type 1 diabetes with minimal human intervention. Selection criteria include the reliability and accuracy of the approaches. Performance evaluation utilizes measures such as mean squared error, mean absolute percentage error, coefficient of determination, and others. The datasets primarily involve type 1 diabetic patients. Preliminary results indicate that some approaches perform well in the short term, while others are effective in the long term, underscoring the importance of extended evaluation. Understanding the strengths and weaknesses of each approach guides future research. This comparison highlights the significance of developing robust prediction methods to enhance type 1 diabetes management. Further research is needed to adapt these approaches to individual patient needs.

articleTitle: In-Vehicle Intrusion Detection based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: The in-vehicle network enables communication between the different vehicle components and systems. It uses specific protocols and bus systems, such as the Controller Area Network (CAN) that provides communication between invehicle parts simultaneously. As the CAN bus plays an essential role in the in-vehicular communication, it is vulnerable to various types of attack, leading to network disconnection and other damage. This paper proposes an intrusion detection system (IDS) based on machine learning that is able to detect and classify CAN messages as DoS, Fuzzy, Spoofing attacks, or normal messages. A comparison between six different algorithms of classification was carried out and found that Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, and Random Forest were the best algorithms, providing excellent results in terms of the evaluation metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, f1-score) as well as the execution time. Thus, the proposed IDS provides a high detection rate to effectively identify most of the attacks and a low computational time to improve the system’s efficiency.

articleTitle: Enhancing Vaccination Strategy Effectiveness in Epidemic Networks: Exploring a New Centrality Measure and Community Detection Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: The prevention and control of infectious diseases heavily rely on vaccination as a crucial strategy. This study introduces an innovative vaccination approach that includes dynamic community detection in an epidemic network, as well as various centrality measures that are compared to a newly proposed centrality measure. Because these measures can identify Super-Spreaders within communities, we prioritize them for vaccination. Our ultimate goal is to create a network of highly immunized people capable of efficiently controlling disease spread. The effectiveness of our method is extensively evaluated utilizing a variety of evaluation metrics. Furthermore, our technique is remarkably scalable and adaptable, making it a promising solution for dealing with future epidemics with varying situations.

articleTitle: Intelligent Hypervisor Placement for VSDN: Adapting to Fluctuating Traffic Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Virtual Software-Defined Networking (VSDN) combines Software-Defined Networking (SDN) and virtualization to offer dynamic provisioning and resource optimization. The critical challenge lies in optimizing hypervisor placement to minimize network latency and ensure efficient resource utilization. In this paper, we present a novel model and dynamic algorithm for hypervisor placement in VSDN. Our approach intelligently assigns hypervisors, adapting to real-time traffic variations. Through simulations, we demonstrate superior performance with lower and stable response times, improving VSDN communication and overall network efficiency. Our algorithm provides consistent and reliable VSDN environments, even with fluctuating traffic scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhanced Traffic Management Through Data Mining: Predictive Models for Congestion Reduction
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: This research focuses on addressing global traffic congestion issues, encompassing safety and emission concerns. A data mining approach is proposed, combining Multiple Linear Regression, Random Forest Classifier, Decision Tree, and XGBRegressor modules to analyze historical traffic data. The aim of this approach is to identify patterns and characteristics, with the ultimate goal of enhancing traffic flow predictions. Experimental validation demonstrates its efficacy, thereby boosting confidence in its potential as a tool for congestion mitigation and road safety improvement. Additionally, this approach aids intelligent transportation systems in proactive decision-making, optimizing traffic management and safety. The utilization of multiple modules allows for a comprehensive analysis of traffic flow data, capturing diverse insights for accurate predictions. The method also integrates temporal aspects by considering traffic patterns, thereby supporting strategies for congestion alleviation and safety enhancement. In conclusion, this research offers a robust data mining solution that integrates various models to accurately predict traffic flow, thereby contributing to safer and less congested travel experiences while assisting traffic management systems.

articleTitle: A LightGBM-Based Approach to improve Sybil Attack Detection in VANET networks
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS) usually rely on Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) to efficiently enable communication and information exchange between vehicles and the infrastructure. However, the openness and dynamic nature of these networks make them vulnerable to security issues. In fact, VANET networks can suffer from several types of attack due to the large number of participants and the homogeneity of the infrastructure. However, we only focus on the Sybil attack that involve malicious entities creating multiple fake identities to disrupt network operations, compromise data integrity, and deceive legitimate vehicles. On the other hand, Machine Learning caught the attention of several researchers in order to solve these security issues, due to it reliability to detect several types of attacks. In this respect, our paper proposes a LightGBM algorithm to detect sybil nodes in VANETs using the position verification approach. When Using the VeReMi dataset, simulations show that the suggested model has better performance when compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: Link prediction in weighted complex networks using machine learning methods and similarity metrics
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: The extensive applicability of social network analysis in capturing social interactions has attracted substantial interest from scholars. One crucial aspect of social network analysis is link prediction, which pertains to estimating the likelihood of a connection between two unconnected nodes within a network. Numerous studies have been conducted to address this problem, and among the existing approaches, similarity-based methods have demonstrated notable efficiency. These methods consider the network’s structure and employ the number of shared neighbors between two nodes as a fundamental measure for establishing structural similarity. When nodes exhibit high structural similarity, it suggests a higher likelihood of a link between them. In this study, two tasks of link prediction are explored. Firstly, the prediction of links in weighted complex networks is investigated using similarity-based metrics. Secondly, link prediction is formulated as a classification task to showcase the efficacy of similarity-based metrics when combined with machine learning models. To evaluate the performance of link prediction metrics, a collection of network-weighted datasets is utilized, and the area under the curve is employed as an evaluation measure. Finally, various supervised learning algorithms are assessed based on their prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: A Novel Centrality based Measure for Influential Nodes Detection in Social Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: The identification of influential actors in social networks plays a crucial role in information dissemination and controlling the spread of rumors and diseases. In this context, social networks can be modeled as graphs, where nodes represent individuals and edges represent their interconnections. Numerous approaches have been proposed in recent years to identify influential actors. In this study, we specifically focus on centrality measures due to their simplicity and efficiency. Structural centrality can be classified into two main methods: local centrality, which is based on the neighborhood of a node, and global centrality, which considers the overall structure of paths between nodes. Another approach involves combining two centrality measures to identify vertices that exhibit high influence at both the local and global levels. Within this paper, we introduce a novel centrality measure that primarily emphasizes the degree of nodes while taking into account the global characteristics of the network, specifically the paths of varying lengths. We evaluate the validity and robustness of the proposed measure using Spearman and Pearson’s correlations on five benchmark datasets. The results of our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed measure in comparison to traditional centrality metrics.

articleTitle: An RFID-Based Traceability Approach to Improve the Overall Health Status Management in Morocco
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Traceability is the ability to verify, follow, manage, and control medical data (or records) that are created during initial consultations in public and private healthcare and hospital centers. As far as Morocco is concerned, these medical records are still created and captured using manual processes and/or traditional electronic systems. These systems are not standardized and can differ among physicians in private centers and even among healthcare institutions. With the advancement of technology, it has become clear that the current trend regarding healthcare is towards common (remotely controlled and) regularly updated digital medical profiles. As a matter of fact, all medical data can be digitized and structured, by developing individual and unique IDs provided for each patient. In this paper, we highlight the importance and benefits of medical traceability and discuss how it can improve and resolve some of the main concerns related to privacy, technology, and systems in Moroccan healthcare. We also introduce a lasting traceability-based approach using RFID to facilitate lifelong health management for Moroccan patients, using a standard and unique ID since birth.

articleTitle: Cooperative Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access for B5G Wireless Networks: Modeling and Simulations
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Beyond 5th-Generation (B5G) systems require massive capacity with low-latency and ubiquitous connectivity. Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) is a potential scheme to meet this requirement by enabling efficient spectrum utilization and user multiplexing. Among the NOMA integration techniques, Cooperative NOMA (C-NOMA) is an innovative technique that can enhance the transmission rate, edge user performance, and spectral efficiency. However, conventional C-NOMA systems have challenges in optimizing user performance. In this article, we address this problem in a downlink C-NOMA system model by employing the Space-Time Block Codes (STBC) approach in a two phase transmission scenario. In the first phase, the NOMA signal is broadcasted by the base station to all users, while in the second phase, the two near users cooperate using the Alamouti code scheme to relay the far user’s signal. We obtain closed-form expressions for the bit error rate for both phases and compare the proposed scheme with the conventional C-NOMA. We use MATLAB to implement the models and analyze the performance of the proposed system in terms of symbol error rate evaluations. The results indicate that STBC-C-NOMA achieves a 2.1 dB gain over conventional C-NOMA. This work provides valuable insights for future research in related C-NOMA fields.

articleTitle: Profiling Language Sign Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Large segments of society place a high value on sign language as a distinct communication language. In computer vision, gesture detection is still a developing phenomenon and a hot topic. Aside from its many applications in immersive game technology and human-computer interaction, gesture recognition has many applications in deaf-mute sign language interpretation. In order to profile language signs, we created a model of image processing that recognizes Arabic hand sign language based on artificial neural networks, starting with the data collection process and continuing with data profiling, then using the deep learning model to train and identify gestures, all the way to the presentation of the results. We offer a method to help with the conversion of sign language into voice and text-based formats. The outcomes we have achieved are crucial, important and significant for our next achievements.

articleTitle: Data Leakage Prevention Approach Based On Insider Trust Calculation
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Nowadays, in the era of technological evolution that the world is currently experiencing, data protection is becoming increasingly important, and keeps coming to the forefront. In this research work, we propose a new layer of detection based on insider’s behavior as well as insider’s trust. The proposed system is based on multi-agent paradigm, which is ideal to threat detection as it can solve the issue of behavioral logs in terms of self-sufficiency and performance. ETL techniques are also employed for data transformation and cleansing. In addition, our method adds a new dimension of analysis based on behavior, taking account of the insider who is the internal employee and his various interactions within the information system.

articleTitle: On The Practicality of Blockchain-based Security and Privacy for Next Generation SDN
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: There has been an increased interest in securing Software Defined Networking (SDN) with Blockchain in recent years. Although Blockchain offers robust defensive security for some applications, its security feature-set does not align well with SDN’s security requirements in a practical setting. This is due to the distributed nature of the state-of-the-art SDN controller services. In this paper, we give a comprehensive architectural analysis of the core Blockchain security feature-set and SDN’s virtualization fabric. Then, we introduce a practical Blockchain-based security and privacy-preserving framework, and discuss the design and implementation of the security services for future generation SDN controllers. This is to entice research on the subject from an architectural prospective.

articleTitle: K-means-dist: A Novel Approach for Enhanced Cybersecurity Clustering Using Combined Distance Metrics
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: In the realm of data analysis and cybersecurity, the development of effective clustering techniques plays a pivotal role in understanding complex datasets and identifying anomalies. This paper presents a novel approach based on an extended K-means algorithm that incorporates both correlation and Euclidean distances to improve clustering performance. The method introduces a combined distance function with customizable distance metric weights to capture diverse data relationships. Applied to a cybersecurity dataset (CIC-IDS2018), traditionally used for supervised Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), we explore unsupervised clustering for IDS, achieving an impressive 92% accuracy. Moreover, our method is adaptable to semi-supervised learning, capturing subtle patterns and relationships in data, making it valuable for various data analysis tasks. This approach has broad applicability for enhancing clustering methodologies across diverse domains.

articleTitle: Ransomware Detection and Classification using Ensemble Learning: A Random Forest Tree Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Viruses significantly threaten computer systems, potentially causing extensive damage and data loss. All users must prioritize cybersecurity by installing effective antivirus software, safeguarding their PCs against potential harm. Even though there are many different kinds of malware, ransomware is particularly dangerous since it prevents victims from accessing their vital data or locks files permanently unless they pay a ransom to the attackers. Recent ransomware strains must be categorized promptly. Data for the present investigation was gathered from a variety of web resources, including Kaggle and ransomware.re. Concerning using Kaggle to acquire harmless datasets, ransomware.re is retrieved for use in a study on ransomware. Many preprocessing methods, such as Normalisation and Imputation, are used to polish our datasets. The most recent additions to the dataset were classified using the Random Forest tree classifier, with a final accuracy of 99.9%. Random Forest Tree fared exceptionally well compared to the KNN and SVM algorithms. We also highlighted that additional preprocessing methods can enhance outcomes for SVM and KNN.

articleTitle: Preserving User Privacy and Empowering Control in Proximity Marketing
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Based on client location, preferences, and behavior data, proximity marketing has become a potent tool for businesses to interact with their target audience in a personalized way. However, questions regarding user control over personal data and privacy are raised by the use of customer tracking, notably through MAC addresses. We suggest a novel algorithm in this paper to improve user control and privacy protection in proximity marketing systems. Our system uses pseudonymous MAC address switching and a consensus-based methodology to give users more protection and control over their interactions. Through simulations and performance criteria including consensus correctness, convergence, and privacy protection, we assess the algorithm’s efficacy. The outcomes show how the algorithm can enhance user control, protect privacy, reduce the likelihood of tracking and profiling, and guarantee computing efficiency for proximity marketing applications. Our findings provide information for further study and practical use, as well as for the creation of privacy-enhancing proximity marketing tactics.

articleTitle: Towards reliability analysis of IEEE 802.11p MAC for platooning in a heterogeneous traffic setup
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: We study the performance of the IEEE 802.11p medium access protocol for platooning of connected vehicles in the presence of interruptions from human-driven Motorised Two Wheelers (MTWs). We invoke specific mobility models for the movement of the vehicles—car-following models for connected vehicle platoons and gap-acceptance model to capture the interruptions by the MTWs—and use them to configure (i) the traffic setup and (ii) the rate at which data packets related to safety-critical messages are generated. A control-theoretic analysis of the car-following models yields a bound on the admissible communication delay to ensure non-oscillatory convergence of the platoon headway. We then use suitable Markov chain models to derive the distribution of the MAC access delay experienced by packets pertaining to safety-critical events as well as routine safety messages. Using the delay distribution and the bound on the admissible delay we compute the reliability of the 802.11p MAC protocol in terms of traffic and protocol parameters. It is seen that the MAC protocol may not always ensure timely delivery of packets for safe platooning. Our study highlights the need for redesign of MAC protocols for vehicular communications in heterogeneous conditions.

articleTitle: Basketball Free Throw Analysis using Object Detection Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: The free throw in basketball is one of the important skills for a player. The accuracy of success of the throw affects the final score in a game, that’s why players make more effort to have a high accuracy in scoring free throw.The studies proved that as a human being, every player has his own way to throw the ball. The player position, the ball shot angle and velocity, are the factors that change from a player to another, and therefore affect the success of the throw even for the same player.The aim of this work is to propose a method to automatically measure and correct the extracted parameters of a basketball free throw shooting. The approach aims to create an automated system to correct the position of basketball throws and track the movement of the ball.

articleTitle: DSP: A Deep Neural Network Approach for Serving Cell Positioning in Mobile Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Positioning remains a crucial aspect with wide-ranging applications, despite the availability of various solutions and extensive research. The lack of transparency surrounding the infrastructure topology and precise locations of base stations operated by telecommunication companies further complicates the positioning process. Moreover, as wireless networks continue to evolve with advancements like 5G and 6G, accurate positioning becomes increasingly important, leveraging vast amounts of data and artificial intelligence techniques. This paper proposes a Deep Neural Network (DNN) based approach called DSP for accurately determining the position of telecommunication operator serving cells in outdoor spaces. The proposed method incorporates fingerprint data collection, machine learning algorithms, and big data analysis to enhance accuracy and expand the range of evaluatable parameters. The data was collected and labeled using the drive test method. By employing deep learning techniques, the proposed method successfully predicts the location of the base station connected to the user device. Through effective data preprocessing and optimized hyperparameters, the average distance error was reduced to 20 meters.

articleTitle: An optimized neural network-based IDS against DDoS attacks
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: As cyberattacks become increasingly sophisticated, the identification of harmful assaults like Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) poses a significant challenge. DDoS attacks have emerged as a critical threat to the safety of information systems and the dependability of computer networks, which serve as vital infrastructures in the contemporary world. Detecting DDoS attacks necessitates a complex undertaking that demands immediate attention to avert substantial damage to networks and services. To tackle this challenge, security researchers propose leveraging the strengths of the Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs) and Neural Network (NN) models to safeguard networks against these threats. However, developing an efficient Neural network-based IDS is not a straightforward task due to the intricate architecture of NN models and the large number of hyper-parameters that need to be tuned. In this context, this paper presents a Neural Network -based IDS for DDoS attacks, employing Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) models optimized using the Bayesian optimization (BO) technique. Experimental results on the CIC-DDoS2019 dataset demonstrate that the CNN achieves an accuracy of 99.71% with a loss value of 0.002. These findings underscore the efficacy of the suggested Intrusion Detection System (IDS) in identifying DDoS attacks within network environments.

articleTitle: Traffic Control, Congestion Management and Smart Parking through VANET, ML, and IoT: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: As the quantity of cars increases on the road, so does the focus on improving road safety and in-vehicle entertainment. In response to this need, the creation of new in-car applications and services is on the rise. Common applications include collision avoidance, safety and traffic monitoring, multimedia streaming, and smart city data collection using wireless sensor networks. The Internet of Things (IOT) is a recent innovation that is accelerating the universe towards automated procedures and intelligent transportation management solutions. This is an important contribution to automation and intelligent civilization. Another way to improve the transport system is through the machine learning (ML). an Existing traffic management solution face a number of problems, resulting in traffic congestion, delays and high fatality rates. In addition, vehicular ad hoc network (VANET) has emerged as a new technology capable of supporting such emerging vehicular applications. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the latest state of the traffic control, traffic management and parking and smart city strategy of the vehicle by using VANET, ML and Internet of Things technology.

articleTitle: SDN Controllers and ML-Based Anomaly Detection in Embedded Systems: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Software-defined networking (SDN) is a novel networking paradigm that decouples the control plane from the data plane, thereby offering enhanced network programmability and flexibility. However, the introduction of SDN has brought forth unique security challenges. This study presents a comprehensive comparative analysis that focuses on the classification of network traffic data derived from a realistic network implementation. The dataset acquired via the REST API from three SDN controllers encompasses diverse network features. The main aim of this study is to employ machine learning algorithms, specifically Decision Tree (DT), Support Vector Machines (SVMs), and Neural Networks (NN), to perform classification tasks on network traffic data. Subsequently, the performance of these algorithms was evaluated in real time using collected network data. The results revealed notable accuracy rates for DT and SVMs, while NN showed improved performance compared with recent studies. Nevertheless, the reaction time for detecting anomalous behaviors is notably compromised across the OpenDaylight (ODL) controller. These findings underscore the significance of comprehending SDN controller performance across various attack and target scenarios when deploying machine learning algorithms for traffic data classification in embedded system networks.

articleTitle: MIMO-NOMA with OSTBC for B5G Cellular Networks with Enhanced Quality of Service
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) scheme has proved a potential candidate to meet the design challenges of orthogonal multiple access (OMA) schemes. High spectrum efficiency and higher data rates are further achieved by integrating NOMA with multiple input multiple output (MIMO) technology. In this article, we have explored orthogonal space-time block coding (OSTBC) to improve the quality of service (QoS) for the proposed MIMO-NOMA framework. We specifically employed the Alamouti STBC scheme, which provides full diversity for the proposed network. At the transmitter side, OSTBC and power domain multiplexing with superposition coding are utilized, while at the reception side, a low complexity maximum likelihood (ML) detector is used, followed by successive interference cancellation (SIC). Based on bit error rate (BER) evaluations, Monte Carlo simulations are performed to analyze the performance of OSTBC MIMO-NOMA system under various fading channels. The proposed framework is further investigated with a higher modulation scheme and different channel code rates. The investigated Alamouti scheme provides a maximum diversity gain of 2M (M shows the number of receiving antennas) without any need for channel state information at the transmitter end and a less complex ML detector at the receiver end. This research lays the groundwork for designing adaptive modulation and coding methods for future MIMO-NOMA based B5G wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Analytical Study for Vehicle Mobility Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: In today’s urbanized world, cities are grappling with new challenges arising from population growth and rapid urbanization. Among these challenges, mobility stands out as a significant concern, as many cities were not initially designed to accommodate the surge in population. Enhancing mobility within smart cities has become a crucial endeavor in order to mitigate traffic congestion and promote sustainability by reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Additionally, improving mobility in smart cities contributes to enhancing the overall quality of life for citizens. Addressing vehicle behavior is crucial in reducing traffic congestion and improving commuting efficiency. Despite having robust infrastructures, disruptive driving habits such as aggressive driving, improper lane usage, and non-compliance with traffic rules can hinder the flow of traffic. By promoting responsible and considerate driving practices, we can optimize traffic flow and create a more efficient and stress-free commuting experience for individuals. Understanding the dynamics of mobility on highways is crucial for identifying the causes of traffic congestion. By analyzing these patterns, valuable insights can be gained, leading to the development of effective solutions for improving traffic flow. This study aims to investigate these aspects and propose strategies to contribute to overall mobility enhancements. To achieve this goal, a novel stochastic model based on the product form that accurately represents overtaking behaviors on highways is presented in this study. The model offers valuable insights into the dynamics of overtaking and provides a comprehensive understanding of this critical aspect of highway traffic. The paper presents a detailed model description and numerical resolution to calculate rewards such as delays and congestion.

articleTitle: Assessing Topic Modeling in Online Forums: A Comparative Study of Hierarchical and Centroid-Based Clustering Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: In the digital age, web forums represent a rich source of textual data waiting to be harnessed for valuable insights. This study aimed to meticulously assess the performance of Hierarchical Latent Dirichlet Allocation (hLDA), Hierarchical Pachinko Allocation (hPA), Hierarchical Dirichlet Process (HDP), and conventional Probabilistic models such as Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA), including their BERT-enhanced versions (LDA-BERT, LSA-BERT). Additionally, we integrated these models with centroid-based (K-Means, K-Means++, Fuzzy C-Means) and hierarchical (Agglomerative Clustering, BIRCH) clustering algorithms. We processed a wide range of documents from diverse web forums, such as TripAdvisor NYC, UbuntuForums, and Photography-on-the.net, and converted them into vectors suitable for each model. The goal of this research is to Methodologically, we applied the models to each dataset and evaluated them based on the aforementioned metrics while assessing the performance of these models using coherence, perplexity, and topic diversity as key performance indicators.. Our results offer crucial insights into the comparative efficiencies of hierarchical and traditional topic models combined with different clustering techniques, specifically within the context of web forum text data.

articleTitle: Visually-Rich Document Understanding: Concepts, Taxonomy and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: The increasing prevalence of Visually-rich Documents (VRDs) in diverse domains has led to a growing interest in Visually-rich Document Understanding (VrDU). Researchers have been developing sophisticated systems to extract explicit and implicit information from such documents. However, a comprehensive literature review on this field still missing. In this paper, we present a comprehensive overview of VrDU systems, focusing on their applications in Key Information Extraction (KIE), Visual Question Answering (VQA) and document classification tasks. We delve into the fundamental concepts and techniques used in VrDU, providing a high-level abstraction of these approaches. To facilitate understanding and comparison, we propose a taxonomy that categorizes VrDU systems based on four key aspects: modality, geometric approach, OCR integration type and task. Additionally, we present the benchmarks commonly used in the field and discuss the current challenges faced by VrDU systems. We believe that this paper advances the research in the field of VrDU by providing a comprehensive resource for researchers and practitioners

articleTitle: Benchmarking Client Selection Methods in Non-IID Federated Learning Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a machine learning technique aimed at collectively acquiring a shared prediction model. When applying FL, the diversity of client data distributions and hardware configurations is a challenge that must be handled. Consequently, randomly sampling clients for training a FL model may not take advantage of the local updates, leading to poor performance of the global model. In this paper, we present a benchmark study in which we evaluate different strategies for worker selection in the context of FL. These strategies can be applied in challenging cases where data exhibits Non-Independent and Identically Distributed (N-IID) characteristics across clients. We select a set of well-known strategies introduced in the literature and performed extensive evaluations according to various scenarios. The obtained results show that there is no fit for all methods for client selection, and the client selection must be selected based on specific criteria.

articleTitle: Future Communication Systems: Toward the Intelligent-based Optimization Approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: The wireless communication systems are expecting to include the high-end service quality for the users and customers. In the last decade, the industry and academia are studying effectively on the sixth generation (6G) systems, since the high performance network connectivity will influence on the number of use cases and also varied applications. For this case, new challenging requirements with key specifications need to be considered deeply for fulfilling the technical drawbacks. In the very recently published papers, it is recognized that researchers focus on solving various problems appeared in the communication systems through advanced optimization methods based on the artificial intelligence (AI). This study devotes to summarize newly and recently published studies where they use optimization and AI-based approaches for tacking their problems related to the communication systems. This review will help readers to discover the suitable AI-based approach for their own challenges.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Data Intensive Applications: Survey
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: This survey article explores recent advancements in data transfers, coflow scheduling, and reducer placement techniques for optimizing the performance of data-intensive applications in computer clusters. These techniques address the challenges of managing data transfers, optimizing resource allocation, and minimizing Coflow Completion Time (CCT). The surveyed research papers present innovative approaches such as intelligent data transfer scheduling, network-aware algorithms, near-optimal heuristics, and leveraging inter-flow relationships. These techniques aim to improve job completion time, enhance resource utilization, and minimize interference in datacenter networks. By summarizing these advancements, this survey article provides a comprehensive overview of the latest research in the field. The findings highlight the significance of these techniques in improving the performance and efficiency of data-intensive applications in computer clusters, and also identifies open challenges and future directions, stimulating further research and development in this area.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Machine Learning-based Load Balancing in High-speed Train System using Nested Cross Validation
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
abstract: Fifth-generation (5G) mobile communication networks have recently emerged in various fields, including high-speed trains. However, the dense deployment of 5G millimeter wave (mmWave) base stations (BSs) and the high speed of moving trains lead to frequent handovers (HOs), which can adversely affect the Quality-of-Service (QoS) of mobile users. As a result, HO optimization and resource allocation are essential considerations for managing mobility in high-speed train systems. In this paper, we model system performance of a high-speed train system with a novel machine learning (ML) approach that is nested cross validation scheme that prevents information leakage from model evaluation into the model parameter tuning, thereby avoiding overfitting and resulting in better generalization error. To this end, we employ ML methods for the high-speed train system scenario. Handover Margin (HOM) and Time-to-Trigger (TTT) values are used as features, and several KPIs are used as outputs, and several ML methods including Gradient Boosting Regression (GBR), Adaptive Boosting (AdaBoost), CatBoost Regression (CBR), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Kernel Ridge Regression (KRR), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and k-Nearest Neighbor Regression (KNNR) are employed for the problem. Finally, performance comparisons of the cross validation schemes with the methods are made in terms of mean absolute error (MAE) and mean square error (MSE) metrics are made. As per obtained results, boosting methods, ABR, CBR, GBR, with nested cross validation scheme superiorly outperforms conventional cross validation scheme results with the same methods.
